The test image shows a split soybean stem with brown/dark discoloration of the internal pith tissue. This is a stem cross-section view. Key features: the pith is darkened/brown throughout, outer stem appears bleached/gray-white, typical of vascular/pith disease.

Top candidates: **Brown_Stem_Rot** (classic brown pith discoloration), **Sudden_death_syndrome** (internal stem browning), **Phytophthora** (stem rot).

**Analysis summary:**

- Test image: Split soybean stem held in hand, showing brown/dark internal pith discoloration, bleached/grayish outer stem — a classic stem cross-section presentation.
- Brown_Stem_Rot ref 103: Near-identical match — split stem, brown pith, same hand-held presentation. BSR is defined by internal brown discoloration of the pith.
- Brown_Stem_Rot ref 18: Shows foliar symptoms (interveinal chlorosis) — a different presentation of the same disease.
- SDS ref 104 and Charcoal_Rot ref 10: Both field-level shots, no stem cross-section, not matching.

The brown pith discoloration in a split stem is the diagnostic signature of Brown Stem Rot (*Cadophora gregata*). The match to reference 103 is very strong.
